purpose: Elapegademase-lvlr is used to treat a rare inherited condition called adenosine deaminase severe combined immunodeficiency, or ADA-SCID. This is a serious disease where the immune system cannot work properly, leaving the body unable to fight off infections. This medication helps replace a missing enzyme so the immune system can function better.
how_it_works: People with ADA-SCID are missing an important enzyme called adenosine deaminase (ADA). Without this enzyme, toxic substances build up in the body and destroy the immune cells that fight infections. This medication is a man-made version of that missing enzyme, and when given by injection, it clears out those toxic substances and helps the immune system rebuild and work properly.
common_side_effects: Injection site reactions such as redness, swelling, or discomfort. You may also experience headache, rash, or mild stomach upset. Some patients notice changes in their lab values, which your doctor will monitor regularly.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have ever had an allergic reaction to any enzyme replacement therapy. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to make sure the medication is working and to watch for any problems. Do not stop taking this medication without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can be very dangerous for your immune system. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection) once a week. The dose is based on your individual lab results and body weight, and your doctor will adjust it over time to make sure it is working at the right level for you.
